correctness.rationale: Every edge-diamond endpoint sum has coordinate counts equal to orientation indegrees after optimal independent signs. A double-cloning identity with strict positive square differences forces uniformity of all within-part rows; an exact edge reversal forbids cyclic part tournaments; adjacent-block swap difference ab(a-b) forces decreasing sizes and lists all maximizers. Symmetric convex-body geometry proves unique ball center and antipodal diameter; strict norm convexity proves exactly the listed contacts. verify.py passed 23 small graph-family partitions, 71,030 orientations, seven full signed endpoint enumerations and six larger nonexhaustive checks. General proof is independent of those finite checks.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating work presents a substantial natural family of cross-polytope Minkowski sums. Exact Euclidean outer spheres and all contact configurations in the complete-multipartite subfamily are genuinely geometric structural invariants, not arbitrary tabular entries. The nontrivial strict sorting law, complete equality classification, and factorial-exponential number of contacts distinguish the edge-diamond geometry from usual graphical zonotopes and extend beyond previously settled cycle graphs. No broad downstream theorem is asserted or required.
